evals.prompt:
Write a GraphQL query for a Jinja2 transform that fetches DcimDevice
with the device's name, its role, and its location's name + shortname.
location is a union of LocationSite | LocationBuilding | LocationHosting
in this repo's base schema. LocationHosting has neither name nor shortname,
so the query must handle the union explicitly so that schema-sync doesn't
fail when a LocationHosting instance is present.
evals.expected_output: A GraphQL query that uses inline fragments (... on LocationSite { ... } and similar) for the location relationship, so fields that exist on some concrete types but not others are scoped to the correct type.
expectations: Inline fragments (... on Location...) are used inside location.node
name and shortname are not selected directly under location.node

assertions.name: query-uses-inline-fragments-for-location
assertions.check: location { node { ... } } contains at least one ... on Location<Type> inline fragment

assertions.name: query-no-direct-field-on-union-location
assertions.check: Neither 'name' nor 'shortname' appears as a direct selection under location.node without an enclosing inline fragment

evals.prompt:
Write a Python async helper named regenerate_and_wait that triggers
regeneration for an Infrahub artifact definition by POSTing to
/api/artifact/generate/<def-id>?branch=<branch>, then waits for completion
by polling CoreArtifact filtered by the definition until at least
`expected_count` instances exist. Time out after 60 seconds and raise
TimeoutError. The helper takes (client, def_id, expected_count, branch)
as parameters.
evals.expected_output: A Python async function that POSTs to /api/artifact/generate/<def-id>, then polls CoreArtifact in a loop until count >= expected_count, with a hard timeout.
expectations: Helper contains a loop (while or for) that waits for completion
Helper polls CoreArtifact via client.filters or client.get with kind='CoreArtifact'
Hard timeout exists (raises after some seconds)

assertions.name: posts-artifact-generate-endpoint
assertions.check: The code calls .post(...) with a URL containing /api/artifact/generate

assertions.name: has-polling-loop
assertions.check: A while/for/async for loop is present (not fire-and-forget)

assertions.name: polls-coreartifact-after-post
assertions.check: A call passes kind="CoreArtifact" (read of artifact state after the POST)

evals.prompt:
I just edited the GraphQL query (queries/device_config.gql) that feeds
my Jinja2 device-config transform — I changed a field selection on the
device's `location` relationship. `infrahubctl schema check` passes and the
YAML is valid, so I'm about to open the PR. Is there anything else I should
run first so I don't hit the silent CoreRepository schema-sync hang? Give me
the concrete commands.

Save your full plan (the commands plus a brief rationale) to: output.md
evals.expected_output: A plan that dry-runs the changed query against a live schema before merge — e.g. `infrahubctl render <transform> --branch <branch>` (or running the check/generator that owns the query) — because static `schema check` and YAML validation do not catch GraphQL/schema mismatches; those only surface when CoreRepository executes the query during schema-sync. The plan should frame this as a pre-merge step.
expectations: Recommends executing the query live as a dry-run via a concrete command (`infrahubctl render`, or `infrahubctl check run` / `infrahubctl generator run`), not just `schema check`
Frames the dry-run as a pre-merge gate (before opening / merging the PR)
Explains that YAML / schema check does not catch GraphQL field or union-fragment mismatches — only live execution does

assertions.name: dry-run-executes-query
assertions.check: Plan dry-runs the query live (infrahubctl render / check run / generator run), not only static schema check

assertions.name: dry-run-before-merge
assertions.check: Plan frames the dry-run as a pre-merge / pre-PR step

evals.prompt:
I want an artifact that delivers a generated **rack elevation
diagram** — an SVG drawing, one per rack. I looked at the transform
examples and they all produce plain text or CSV, so I assumed
artifacts can only carry text and that I would have to serve the
diagram some other way.

Can an artifact deliver a diagram? If it can, build it: the
transform and the registration. Each rack has a `height` in rack
units and `devices` with a `position` and a `device_type.height`.

I already compute the geometry as a dict (`{"width": 220,
"height": 900, "slots": [{"y": 40, "h": 40, "label": "leaf-01"}]}`),
so just return that dict from the transform and let Infrahub render
it as the drawing. Keep the transform short.

Save the transform to: output.py
Save the `.infrahub.yml` registration to: output.md
evals.expected_output: A confirmation that artifacts do support diagrams, an `artifact_definitions` entry with `content_type: image/svg+xml`, and a transform whose `transform` method returns a **string** of SVG markup. The requested dict return is refused and the geometry is rendered into markup instead: only application/json and application/yaml serialise a dict, every other content type passes the payload through str(), so the dict would be stored as its Python repr with no error.
expectations: Confirms an artifact can carry a diagram; image/svg+xml is one of the eight supported content types
The artifact definition declares content_type image/svg+xml
Refuses to return the geometry dict and renders it into an SVG string instead, annotated -> str
States that only application/json and application/yaml serialise a dict, and that other types go through str()
The target group's node inherits CoreArtifactTarget on the concrete node

assertions.name: artifact-content-type-declared
assertions.check: The artifact definition declares content_type image/svg+xml

assertions.name: svg-transform-returns-str
assertions.check: The transform returns a string, not the geometry dict, whether returned as a literal or through a local variable

assertions.name: svg-markup-in-output
assertions.check: The source builds real SVG markup: an <svg root element and the svg namespace
